commons:61148088.summary: This fragment of a woven tunic ornament, in wool and linen tapestry, is laid out as a band of square panels filled with rosettes and birds. In the central roundel a small frontal figure with a round head and dark hair appears half-length, possibly flanked by wings. The Met's own title proposes, with a question mark, that the ornament showed Christ and the Virgin flanked by angels; in its present fragmentary state the figure cannot be securely identified.
facts: This fragment (acc. 90.5.818) came to the Met in 1890 as a gift of George F. Baker.
commons:61148088.notes: Met object 444297, dated 7th–8th century, Islamic Art department. Identification of Christ rests only on the Met's tentative title; the visible figure could be the Virgin, an angel or another figure. Scripture omitted. Not a duplicate of met:444058 (a different fragment, 90.5.579, with the same title).

cur:catacombs-mp-adoration-magi.summary: Wilpert's plate shows a whole painted chamber: in the arcosolium at the back the Magi bring their gifts to the Virgin and Child, while the surrounding walls and ceiling carry orantes, Jonah, Moses striking the rock and Noah in the ark. The Epiphany is set among Old Testament images of deliverance, as the first revelation of Christ to the nations.
facts: According to the Commons description, the scenes from top are orants, Jonah and the whale, Moses striking the rock, Noah praying in the ark and the Adoration of the Magi.
Painting reproduced from Joseph Wilpert, Die Malereien der Katakomben Roms (Freiburg, 1903), whose plates were photographed in the catacombs and hand-coloured in front of the originals.

cur:catacombs2-british-museum-gold-glass.summary: A husband in a richly folded toga and a wife wearing a jewelled necklace are shown side by side in this cracked gold-glass medallion. Between and above them stands a small figure of Christ, who holds a wreath over each of their heads, blessing their marriage, while an inscription runs around the border. Such glasses were probably wedding gifts, and many were later set into the walls of graves in the catacombs.
facts: Married couples crowned by a small figure of Christ are a recurrent Christian adaptation of the Roman marriage portrait on 4th-century gold glass; another example is in the Bargello, Florence.
Commons classes it among gold-glass portraits showing the toga contabulata, the folded toga of the later Roman Empire.
cur:catacombs2-british-museum-gold-glass.notes: The inscription is only partly legible and is not transcribed; the British Museum's registration details were not verified.

cur:objects-tassilo-chalice.summary: On the cup of this great chalice an oval medallion shows Christ in half-length, blessing and holding a book, flanked by the letters alpha and omega and the initials of 'Iesus Salvator'; four further medallions show the evangelists with their symbols. Interlace and animal ornament cover the rest of the vessel. Raised at the altar, the chalice placed the image of Christ the Saviour directly above the wine of the Eucharist.
facts: Wikipedia notes that the chalice was donated by Liutperga, wife of the Bavarian duke Tassilo III, possibly when Kremsmünster Abbey was founded in 777; the inscription round the foot reads TASSILO DUX FORTIS + LIVTPIRG VIRGA REGALIS.
It stands 25.5 cm high and holds about 1.75 litres; although synods forbade copper and bronze for consecrated chalices, it is one of the few surviving examples of such vessels.
cur:objects-tassilo-chalice.notes: Photographed while on loan to the exhibition 'Charlemagne – Power, Art, Treasures' at the Centre Charlemagne, Aachen.
